target_customer: Coffee roasters and buyers that pay a fixed fee per pound to have smallholder farms verified against sustainability standards (nonprofit)
problem: Certification labels are expensive and reach few smallholder farmers, so buyers cannot see social, environmental and economic conditions across their supply chains.
business_model: Nonprofit that began on grants and charges coffee companies a fixed fee per pound verified
product_category: Supply chain sustainability verification using surveys, satellite imagery and machine learning

founders.name: David Browning
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2018-08-30) says he led TechnoServe's global coffee practice and founded Enveritas in 2016.

founders.name: Carl Cervone
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (2018-08-30) names him as co-founder; says he advised coffee growers in Africa, Asia and Latin America at TechnoServe. Not listed on the YC page.

competitors.name: Rainforest Alliance and Fair Trade certification
competitors.what: Certification labels the company positions itself against as costly and reaching few producers
competitors.traction_then: Described as covering only a small fraction of producers

technical_complexity.rationale: Mixed model of large field survey operations across 10 countries plus geospatial analysis and machine learning to find farms; operations were harder than the software.

defensibility.rationale: Farm level survey data and in-country survey teams built over years are slow to replicate, though the verification concept is not patented.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Certifiers kept operating alongside; no incumbent copied or acquired Enveritas through 2026 and it keeps growing with named roaster partners.

market_need_then: Roasters faced pressure to show responsible sourcing while certifications covered few producers and cost farmers money. The team scaled to 10 countries in about 1.5 years per its 2018 MIT Solve page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Impact oriented, mission language such as ending poverty in coffee by 2030

branding.brand_signature: Enveritas Green responsibly sourced verification claim used by roaster partners
branding.community_and_virality: Roaster partners such as San Francisco Bay Coffee and Peets publish partner pages about the verification.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within the coffee trade through partner pages but no consumer brand pull and name origin not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Enveritas is a nonprofit started by two former TechnoServe coffee specialists. It began on grants, including a Gates Foundation agriculture grant, and moved to a revenue model where coffee companies pay per pound verified, reporting 2018 revenue of 7.5 million dollars in its own application. It later reported covering most global coffee production and added government and EUDR work. No exit, shutdown or layoffs were found.
notes: The company website returned 403 so only search snippets from it were used. Gates grant amount and date are not stated. CB Insights labels latest round Seed and Dealroom shows 0 to 10M disclosed equity; both are aggregators and not recorded. The 7.5 million 2018 revenue figure is self-reported on MIT Solve. Only the YC page lists David Browning; Carl Cervone is from TechCrunch.
